newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Strike postponement seen good for Seoul bourse.
newsitem.headline: Strike postponement seen good for Seoul bourse.

text.p: The postponement of a four-hour general strike on Friday will be a positive factor for the Korea Stock Exchange, brokers said.
But the labour situation has not been resolved and the general trend continues to be weak, so the composite stock index could move sideways during the day, they said.
The composite index was down 2.17 percent, or 15.30 points, to a close of 689.38 on Thursday.
"Of course there will be a positive effect, because there was expectatioon of conflict between management and labour," said Seoul Securities broker Park Hae-soo.
The outlawed Korea Confederatin of Trade Unions said they would postpone the threatened strike because they did not feel a controversial labour bill would be passed by parliament.

On Thursday, opposition parties called for a delay in pushing through the bill that allows layoffs and flexible work hours. The ruling New Korea Party wants to adopt the bill during the current session of parliament, which ends on December 18.
Brokers said they expected a rebound in shares that had been hit by selling on Thursday by institutions trying to maximise future trading gains.

Brokers said because Thursday was the settlement date for December futures contracts, institutions holding short positions on the index futures trading put a huge amount of sell orders to maximise gains.
Blue chips are expected to see some bargain hunting. Shares affected by mergers and acquisition talks, such as Koram Bank, would also be in focus, traders said.
